questions.question: What does ABS help you do?

options.text: Lock up the wheels.
Stop the wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.
Predict the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What should NOT be part of a post-trip inspection?

options.text: Looking for items left on the bus.
Checking for sleeping students.
Opening windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening windows.
questions.explanation: After a trip, check for sleeping students and lost items. Also look for open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage. Opening windows is not part of the inspection.

questions.question: Which situation causes the most student deaths per year?

options.text: Students loading and unloading a school bus
Accidents with drunk drivers
Accidents caused by careless driving
Accidents from ignoring traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students loading and unloading a school bus
questions.explanation: More students die getting on or off school buses than riding inside them.

questions.question: What should you do if a student is missing after exiting the bus?

options.text: Park the bus safely and look for the student.
Assume the student got off safely.
Walk to the back of the bus to see if they got back on.
Ask another student if they've seen them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the bus safely and look for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot find a student after they exit, park the bus and check around and underneath it for the missing student.

questions.question: What gear should you use when stopping to pick up students?

options.text: Park.
First gear.
Reverse.
Third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park.
questions.explanation: Put the bus in park when stopping to pick up students. If there is no park gear, use neutral.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The brake pedal should stick.
The gas pedal should be loose.
The grooved pedal surface should not be worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface should not be worn smooth.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that nothing blocks the pedals and that they work properly. The pedal surfaces should be grooved for safety.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In pairs.
Without using the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line and use the handrail for safety.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must:

options.text: Keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
Turn to face the road before you finish exiting.
Face away from the vehicle.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle when exiting and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, stay in contact with the handrail. Wrong exit technique can fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror used for?

options.text: Watch passengers.
See potential hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.
See in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is used to watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
Within five feet of where the examiner said.
Anywhere you can park safely.
Within two feet of where the examiner said.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you to park it.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner describes. Not parking exactly where instructed will lower your score on the basic control skills test.

questions.question: How should passengers exit a school bus in an emergency?

options.text: Always use the back door.
Use whichever exit is safest.
Always use the front door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever exit is safest.
questions.explanation: When evacuating a school bus, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest for passengers to use.

questions.question: How many seconds before a bus stop should you turn on warning lights?

options.text: One to two seconds
Two to four seconds
Five to ten seconds
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Five to ten seconds
questions.explanation: Turn on amber warning lights at least 200 feet (about five to ten seconds) before the stop.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Drive straight forward, then back straight up.
Back straight up, then drive forward to the left.
Drive straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: First drive straight forward. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up at a student pick-up point?

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Let all students board first, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up to meet the other half.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all students board first, then back up.
questions.explanation: Wait until all students have boarded the bus before backing up. Always watch for students who arrive late.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up at a student pick-up point?

options.text: Back up before students board the bus.
Let students board the bus, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up toward the other half.
Tell students to wait and then back toward the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let students board the bus, then back up.
questions.explanation: Pick up all students before backing up the bus. Watch carefully for latecomers when backing.

questions.question: What should you do during the on-road driving test?

options.text: Choose your own route to show your driving skills.
Follow the examiner's directions.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.
Drive unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the examiner's directions.
questions.explanation: Listen to and follow the examiner's directions during the test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when students are boarding?

options.text: Tell students when it is safe to board.
Count students to make sure everyone has boarded.
Let students board in pairs.
Check mirrors for students rushing toward the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let students board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Students must board in a single-file line, not in pairs.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help you see?

options.text: The danger zones at the front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones at the front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors let you see the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: What should you NOT do during the on-road driving test?

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without any accidents.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Drive safely. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without any accidents or traffic violations.
